note: Official 2026–27 WPI catalog and current Michigan department pages checked October 14, 2026. These describe current requirements and catalog eligibility, not guaranteed Fall 2027 schedules, seats or research placements. Michigan bulletin/CSE pages returned 403; the official admissions knowledge base still states that CS selection is required.

wpi.total_credits: Use WPI units; the entries below show verified major distribution requirements, not a standalone audit of every university graduation requirement. [W1]
wpi.credit_or_unit_system: Courses commonly carry 1/3 unit; catalog rotation Category I = at least annually, Category II = at least every other year. [W1][W5][W6]
wpi.elective_structure: At least 1 unit of Engineering Science & Design electives, with at least 2/3 unit at 4000-level or above. Choose robotics AI courses within approved degree/elective rules; no named ML course is mandatory. [W1]
wpi.declaration_gate: University admission, then major declaration near the end of first-year B-Term. No separate competitive RBE major gate is published on the reviewed pages. [W9]
wpi.flexibility: BS AI with a Robotics concentration is a different degree; RBE plus carefully selected AI electives preserves required robotics engineering depth. [W1][W11]
wpi.size: Current major-specific enrollment and class sizes were not reverified.
distinctive: Required four-course Unified Robotics sequence integrates mechanics, sensors, manipulation and navigation. [W1]
RBE 3001 builds and programs a vision-guided robotic manipulator; RBE 3002 uses an open-ended term navigation problem. [W2][W3]
RBE 2020 combines robot electronics, microcontrollers and a hands-on electronic subsystem lab; it can satisfy embedded systems. [W4]
RBE 4744 is an undergraduate deep-learning course with vision transformers, diffusion models, sim2real and adversarial attacks. [W6]
The Robotics Engineering BS is EAC-ABET accredited under General Criteria. [W10]

Within at least 2/3 unit ECE; RBE 2020 can satisfy this component
Object-oriented programming and software engineering required
At least 1/3 unit each; RBE 502 cannot satisfy classical controls
Differential/integral calculus, differential equations, linear algebra and probability
Must be a Capstone Design Experience in Robotics Engineering
At least 2/3 unit at 4000-level or above
At least 1/3 unit each; university breadth and project requirements also apply

capstone.what: The MQP must be a Capstone Design Experience in Robotics Engineering. A required project does not guarantee an industry sponsor, research lab placement or co-op employment. [W1]

wpi.ai_ml: Undergraduate choices: RBE 4701 AI for Robotics (search, uncertainty, RL, deep learning; Category II); RBE 4744 Deep Learning for Perception (Category I); RBE 4540 Vision-based Manipulation (Category I); CS 4342 ML (Category I). Their recommended background includes programming, linear algebra, probability and, for some choices, calculus/differential equations or algorithms. [W5][W6][W7][W8]
wpi.hands_on: Required manipulation and navigation lab sequence; RBE 2020 robot electronics; classical controls; RBE capstone MQP. WPI labels course preparation as recommended background; do not silently convert it to an enforced prerequisite. [W1][W2][W3][W4]

umich.credit_or_unit_system: Semester credits; ROB 310, 311, 314, 320, 330, 340 and 450 are 4-credit courses on the current list. [M2]
umich.elective_structure: 18 technical-elective credits, including at least 6 credits from two upper-level ROB courses. Five optional concentrations use at least 12 credits already within the degree. Additional core choices can count as flexible technical electives. [M1]
umich.declaration_gate: CoE admission, one completed Ann Arbor term, GPA at least 2.0 and good standing, and C or better/exam/transfer credit in linear algebra, design or programming, calculus, and physics or chemistry; then a declaration appointment. [M1]
umich.flexibility: Three of six core choices allow specialization, but hardware and controls are optional choices. Full Stack requires all six plus two courses from different concentrations. CS remains separately selected according to the current official admissions knowledge base. [M1][M4]
umich.size: Current course capacity and major-specific admission rates were not reverified.
distinctive: Current core table explicitly includes ROB 314: choose three of six, not five. Older prose on the same page still says five. [M1]
Choose ROB 310/311 for physical hardware and ROB 314 for controls, then ROB 330 for autonomy through an additional core/elective choice. [M1][M2]
ROB 429 Robot Learning and ROB 430 Deep Learning are expressly marked undergraduate upper-level electives; use these rather than assuming every graduate course is open. [M2]
Optional Full Stack concentration covers all six core areas; Perception and Reasoning includes ROB 330 and EECS 442/ROB 432. [M1]
SURE is a selected summer research opportunity after sophomore/junior study; current Summer 2026 page lists 10–12 weeks and $6,000. Future dates are unknown. [M5]

required_core.title: Sensors/signals; build/motion; controls; operating systems; localization/mapping/navigation; HRI
At least 6 credits from two upper-level ROB courses, plus flexible technical electives
Common CoE math/science/programming and breadth requirements; total degree 128 credits

capstone.what: ROB 450 is a 4-credit team-based senior major design project; the department course list labels it Winter. ROB 490 research can count for up to 4 flexible-elective credits via faculty proposal and petition, not as an upper-level elective. [M1][M2]

umich.ai_ml: ROB 429 Robot Learning for Planning and Control (3 credits, Winter); ROB 430 Deep Learning for Robot Perception and Manipulation (4, Winter); ROB 422/EECS 465 Algorithmic Robotics (3, Fall/Winter); EECS 442/ROB 432 Computer Vision is a concentration core. Undergraduate elective eligibility is documented; individual enforced prerequisites and seats still need checking. [M1][M2]
umich.hands_on: Hardware depth depends on core choices: ROB 310 sensors/signals, ROB 311 robot building/motion, ROB 314 controls and ROB 330 navigation. ROB 450 integrates the degree in a senior project. [M1][M2]

shared_ground: Both are dedicated undergraduate robotics degrees with computing, electronics and mechanical foundations. [W1][M1]
Both require a major design project: RBE MQP at WPI and ROB 450 at Michigan. [W1][M1]
Neither requires an introductory ML course by name; the AI depth depends on elective selection and preparation. [W1][M1]
Published course eligibility and research programs do not guarantee a seat or lab placement. [W5][W6][M2][M5]

differences.dimension: Required building versus chosen core depth
differences.wpi: Four Unified Robotics courses are required; manipulation and navigation contain substantial lab projects. [W1][W2][W3]
differences.umich: ROB 204 plus three of six core courses. ROB 310/311/314 are deliberate hardware/controls choices, and additional core courses can use elective slots. [M1]
differences.why_it_matters_for_a_robotics_ai_job: For a balanced robotics goal, preserve actual hardware and control experience alongside perception and autonomy electives.

differences.wpi: RBE 4701, 4744 and 4540 plus CS 4342 offer robotics AI, deep perception, manipulation and ML in the undergraduate catalog. [W5][W6][W7][W8]
differences.umich: ROB 429/430/422 and EECS 442/ROB 432 support robot learning, deep perception, planning and vision. [M1][M2]
differences.why_it_matters_for_a_robotics_ai_job: Use a prepared elective sequence. A long graduate course list is not evidence of easy undergraduate access.

differences.wpi: RBE 4701 is Category II (at least every other year); 4744/4540/CS 4342 are Category I (at least annually). WPI publishes recommended background. [W5][W6][W7][W8]
differences.umich: Current department labels 310 Winter; 311/314/330 Fall; 429/430/450 Winter. Individual prerequisites and seat restrictions require a further check. [M2]
differences.why_it_matters_for_a_robotics_ai_job: Catalog rotation is useful planning evidence, not a guarantee of a particular future semester.

differences.wpi: Admitted to WPI, then prompted to declare near the end of first-year B-Term; no separately selective RBE gate published on reviewed pages. [W9]
differences.umich: Apply to CoE, then meet one-term, GPA and four foundation-category requirements. CS has separate selection. [M1][M4]
differences.why_it_matters_for_a_robotics_ai_job: Distinguish university admission, major declaration and course enrollment instead of calling both degrees direct admit.

differences.wpi: At least 1 unit ES&D electives with 2/3 at 4000-level or above; use current catalog requirements to place AI courses. [W1]
differences.umich: 18 technical-elective credits; optional concentrations give structure without adding degree credits. Full Stack requires all six core courses plus two from different concentrations. [M1]
differences.why_it_matters_for_a_robotics_ai_job: Michigan can formalize broad systems depth; WPI embeds its four-course unified sequence in the required program.

admission.wpi: Apply to the university and indicate an intended major. Major declaration is prompted near the end of B-Term in the first year; students still exploring receive faculty advising. No reviewed official page publishes an RBE-specific admission or GPA selection gate. [W9]
admission.umich: First-year robotics applicants apply to the College of Engineering. Declaring Robotics requires one full Ann Arbor term, overall GPA ≥2.0, good standing and C-or-better/exam/transfer credit in each of four foundation categories. No competitive Robotics selection is published on this page. Official admissions guidance still states selection for CS in both LSA and Engineering; the claim that it was removed in Spring 2026 was not verified. [M1][M3][M4]
